A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Text, equations, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original autoencoder and RNN experiments in Figures 1–5, with additional experimental analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds numerical optimisation results under imperfect reconstruction in Appendix E and Figure 12.

M1.justification: The proposed architectures, nonnegativity constraints and energy objectives are retained. Appendix E varies reconstruction weighting in a supplementary experiment without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds a controlled rare-corner scenario: four square-corner points with one occurring with probability 0.01. The existing synthetic-source, what-where, Isaac3D, recurrent and navigation task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The comparison methods are retained, including networks with and without biological constraints. New Figure 12 compares reconstruction weights within the same model rather than adding a comparator.

E3.justification: The new experiment compares reconstruction-to-regularisation weight ratios of 10^6 and 10^5 on a fixed rare-corner distribution (Figure 12). Settings and metrics for the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix E tests sensitivity to the perfect-reconstruction assumption by lowering the reconstruction penalty. This adds a focused robustness analysis alongside the retained corner-cutting, correlation and biological-constraint analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds for what-where experiments and standard-error shading in Figure 2. v3 introduces no additional repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New Figure 12 reports modular, axis-aligned representations at the higher reconstruction penalty and mixed representations at the lower penalty. Previously reported experimental findings and plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem B.4 changes from a local-optimality criterion to a global-optimality statement. New Appendix B.5 supplies a Gram-matrix convexity argument and claims uniqueness of the optimal representational similarity matrix; the existing convex-hull proof moves to B.6.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and main conclusion retain the same headline contributions: source-support conditions for modularity, empirical generalisation to nonlinear networks, and explanations of neural coding observations.

C2.justification: Section 6 and new Appendix E explicitly explain that allowing reconstruction errors can make networks disregard rare extremal points, qualifying the applicability of the support-based theory. v2 did not discuss this failure condition.

D1.justification: Appendix E and Figure 12 disclose the new experiment's sampling probabilities and loss-weight ratios. Existing implementation details, hardware descriptions and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The convexity argument adds references to Berman and Shaked-Monderer, Boyd and Vandenberghe, and Sengupta et al., plus attribution to Robert Israel. The broader related-work positioning is retained; publication updates to existing references do not add distinct studies.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited prose corrections, revises the discussion, adds acknowledgements and adopts author-year citations. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact, with new appendix sections inserted.

P2.justification: The document-wide switch to ICLR formatting changes margins, typography, headers, figure scaling and placement. A new three-panel Figure 12 is added; existing figure graphics are retained and redistributed through the revised layout.

improvement.justification: Appendix E and the revised limitations usefully clarify when reconstruction errors undermine modularity. However, v3 replaces v2's local-optimality caveat with a global guarantee whose new proof has an unresolved rank issue: Equation 93 uses D^-1 although D = Z^T Z can be singular when K > d_s + 1. The empirical clarification and unresolved rigor of the strengthened theorem prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
